name: Flax-Flower Blossom
lede: Flax-Flower Blossom is a dusty, moderate blue named for the small sky-colored flowers of the flax plant, first recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1930 and distinguished from its closest neighbor by being a shade bluer.

sections.title: A flax-blue
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records this hue at plate 36 F 7, with a first recorded date of 1705 [1]. The flax plant's flowers, which give us linen and linseed oil, open a pale, clear blue; this name takes that flower's color and pushes it a step darker and greyer, into what the ISCC-NBS system would call a moderate blue [2]. In Munsell terms it sits near 2.8PB 4.3/4.9: low chroma, tipped toward violet [2].

The nearest named color is [[queen-blue|Queen Blue]], 3.0 units away and more vivid; [[dark-cadet-blue|Dark Cadet Blue]] sits almost on top of it, 3.9 units off, in nearly the same place [2]. Maerz and Paul's own plate also carries Orient Blue, Firmament and Milano Blue as later variants on the same page [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Flax-Flower Blossom appears in 204 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed, more common than 59 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 26 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.8 times the expected rate for that century, and is most over-represented in French paintings, at 2.2 times expected [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, tucked into shadow rather than carrying the light [3]. The earliest match is dated 1405, 525 years before Maerz and Paul's 1930 record of the name — a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of the flax dye itself, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].
